newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita unit develops 64 megabit flash chip.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita unit develops 64 megabit flash chip.

text.p: Matsushita Electronics Corp, wholly owned by Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, said on Wednesday that it and SanDisk Corp of the United States had developed a multi-state 64 megabit flash chip.
Matsushita Electronics said it would be the first semiconductor maker to start mass production of the chip, but it did not say when production would begin.
The chip can store a large amount of data and is cost-efficient, Matsushita said.
Demand for flash products with larger capacity, lower power consumption and lower cost is rising due to increased use of digital equipment, it said.
Matsushita Electronics will ship all its flash chips to SanDisk, which will produce flash disc cards with the chips, it said.
Matsushita Electronics and SanDisk have been cooperating on development of flash memory since 1990.
